name: What shower waterproofing questions should I ask before signing a contract?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a bathroom contractor will waterproof the shower correctly?
mainEntity.text: How do I know if a bathroom contractor will waterproof the shower correctly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waterproofing is one of the most important parts of a bathroom remodel, yet it is often the least visible. Before signing, ask the contractor which waterproofing system they use, how the shower pan is sloped, how seams and penetrations are treated, and whether they flood-test the pan before tiling. Tile and grout alone are not waterproof, so the underlying membrane or pan assembly matters most. You should also ask who is responsible for the waterproofing if another trade installs part of the shower. In Los Angeles homes, where showers are used heavily and hidden moisture damage can be expensive, a clear waterproofing plan is essential. A contractor who cannot explain the process in plain language is a red flag.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask what waterproofing system they use, how the shower pan is built, whether corners and penetrations are sealed, and how long the waterproofing is cured before tile is installed. A proper shower build should include a continuous waterproof layer, not just tile and grout.
